panels.title: Scrape targets down
panels.description: Any target Prometheus cannot reach, in any namespace.

panels.title: Flux controllers up
panels.description:
Scraped controllers as a fraction of the controller Deployments that exist, so the tile survives Flux gaining or losing one - enabling image-automation-controller, for instance, would silently break a hardcoded count of 4.

The denominator is count(), not sum(), of kube_deployment_spec_replicas - the opposite of the application tiles on Alert status. There the desired replica count IS the expectation: scaling ml-api to one replica means 1/1 is healthy. A Flux controller scaled to zero is not a capacity decision, it is an outage, and sum() hides it by dropping numerator and denominator together. Measured with notification-controller scaled to 0: sum() still read 100%, count() correctly read 75%.

It also counts every Deployment in flux-system, which holds only Flux's own controllers. kube-state-metrics does not expose app.kubernetes.io/part-of by default, so a precise join would need metricLabelsAllowlist.

The four named tiles below cover today's controllers; one that appears later has no tile of its own but shows up here and in 'Targets that are down'.

panels.title: Flux reconcile errors (15m)
panels.description: Errors are per controller, not per resource - Flux v2.9 exposes no per-resource readiness metric. See docs/observability.md.

panels.title: Flux resources not Ready
panels.description:
Per-resource readiness, via kube-state-metrics reading the Flux CRs. Excludes suspended resources.

Sorted by Suspended descending, so anything suspended floats to the top instead of hiding somewhere in the middle of the list.

panels.description: Flat at zero for a kind means that controller has stopped working through its queue.

panels.title: Flux resources and readiness
panels.description:
From gotk_resource_info. A resource absent here is not known to kube-state-metrics at all.

Suspended resources are highlighted: a suspended Kustomization keeps its last Ready=True condition, so the green Ready column alone hides the fact that nothing is reconciling it any more.

Sorted by Suspended descending, so anything suspended floats to the top instead of hiding somewhere in the middle of the list.

panels.title: Kubernetes events
panels.description:
Events for everything outside the application namespaces - the monitoring stack, Flux, kube-system. Application events are on Alert status. Written as a negation, so an unclassified namespace shows up here rather than nowhere.

Kubernetes drops events after about an hour; Alloy ships them to Loki so they outlive the incident that produced them.

Narrow with `| json | type = "Warning"` or `| json | reason =~ "Killing|Unhealthy|BackOff|Failed"`.
